chunks: From him, from al-Barqi, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, who said:

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the prey of the falcon and the hawk when it kills its prey and the man watches it. He said, 'Eat from it, even if it has also eaten something from it.' I repeated the question to him three times, and each time he said the same. The reason for the interpretation of these narrations is taqiyyah (dissimulation), which we have mentioned, because the rulers of the time considered it permissible and their jurists issued fatwas regarding its permissibility. Thus, the narrations came in accordance with them, as they came in similar cases. And that which indicates this is what was narrated:

key_terms.صَيْدِ الْبَازِي وَالصَّقْرِ: prey of the falcon and the hawk

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat the prey of a falcon or hawk if it has already eaten some of it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) confirms the permissibility of consuming prey caught by falcons or hawks, even if the bird has already eaten part of it. The accompanying commentary attributes this ruling to *taqiyyah* (dissimulation), noting that it aligned with the prevailing judicial practices and fatwas of the Umayyad or Abbasid rulers and their jurists to avoid political friction. This highlights the dynamic interplay between religious law and socio-political realities in Shia jurisprudence.
